coverage.note: Section heading for FR1.1-FR1.5; traceability is carried by the member rows.
validateCreate enforces the required fields and the category enum.
model, notes and assigned_to are stored as optional fields.
UNIQUE (category, serial_or_key); duplicates raise DUPLICATE_ASSET.
A successful registration redirects to /assets, where the new asset is listed.
Every new row is persisted with a random UUID, created_at/updated_at timestamps and status 'in-stock'. The schema default is in src/db/migrations.sql.
Section heading for FR2.1-FR2.5; traceability is carried by the member rows.
Columns: name, category, serial/key, status, assigned to.
listAssets searches LOWER(name) and LOWER(serial_or_key).
listAssets filters by category and by status.
listAssets sorts by name or created_at, ascending or descending.
Each row links to /assets/:id.
Section heading for FR3.1-FR3.3; traceability is carried by the member rows.
The details grid lists every asset field, including the assignment and return timestamps.
The audit section renders the most recent audit entry.

The actions section renders only the forms valid for the asset's current state: in-stock offers assign; assigned offers return and mark-lost; returned offers mark-lost and re-assign; lost offers none. `returned -> returned` is not a valid transition, so no 'Mark returned' form is offered for a returned asset.
Section heading for FR4.1-FR4.8; traceability is carried by the member rows.
The TRANSITIONS map defines the four states.
in-stock -> assigned only.
assigned -> returned or lost.
returned -> assigned or lost.
lost has an empty transition set and is terminal.
assignAsset records the assignee name and the assigned_at timestamp.
returnAsset clears the assignee and records the returned_at timestamp.
updateAsset always writes updated_at.
Section heading for FR5.1-FR5.3; traceability is carried by the member rows.
recordAudit appends timestamp, action type and description.
The most recent entry is rendered in the audit section.
The full audit log is deliberately not exposed in the UI for the poc; only the most recent entry is shown, on views/detail.ejs.
The list view links directly to the registration form, so registration is 1 click away.

Case-insensitive search over name and serial_or_key returns a filtered list on request. No supporting index exists: the search is a leading-wildcard `LIKE`, which would not use a B-tree index even if one were created.
npm start boots the app with embedded SQLite only.
Documented setup steps for a single Linux/macOS host.
WAL journalling, foreign keys on, and a single-writer SQLite file.
Only the free-text assignee name is stored; nothing is sent to an external service.
README documents install, start and test steps.
